name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q07 - Cytoskeleton ciliary axoneme array and centriolar hub

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: The cytoskeleton in eukaryotic cells consists of an elaborate network of microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments involved in mechanical support, motility, and shape maintenance.

Statement II: The axoneme of cilia and eukaryotic flagella possesses a 9 + 2 array of microtubules, consisting of nine pairs of peripheral doublets and two central singlet microtubules.

Statement III: Centrioles possess an axonemal core identical to cilia, consisting of nine peripheral doublets and a central sheath.

Statement IV: The central proteinaceous rod of the centriole is called the hub, which is connected to peripheral triplets by radial spokes.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: यूकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में कोशिकीय कंकाल (साइटोस्केलेटन) में सूक्ष्मनलिकाओं, सूक्ष्मप्रतंतुओं और मध्यवर्ती तंतुओं का विस्तृत जाल होता है जो यांत्रिक सहारा, गति और आकार बनाए रखने में शामिल होता है।

कथन II: पक्ष्माभ (सिलिया) और यूकैरियोटिक कशाभ (फ्लैजिला) के अक्षसूत्र में सूक्ष्मनलिकाओं का 9 + 2 विन्यास होता है, जिसमें नौ परिधीय युग्मक (डबलेट्स) और दो केंद्रीय एकल नलिकाएं होती हैं।

कथन III: तारककेंद्रों (सेंट्रिओल्स) का आंतरिक अक्षसूत्र सिलिया के समान होता है, जिसमें नौ परिधीय युग्मक और एक केंद्रीय आवरण पाया जाता है।

कथन IV: तारककेंद्र की केंद्रीय प्रोटीनयुक्त छड़ को धुरी (हब) कहा जाता है, जो अरीय दंडों (रेडियल स्पोक्स) द्वारा परिधीय त्रिकों (ट्रिपलेट्स) से जुड़ी होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The eukaryotic cytoskeleton provides structural integrity and motility through specialized tubulin assemblies organized either into axonemal 9+2 doublets (cilia/flagella) or 9+0 triplets (centrioles).

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding cytoskeletal elements: The cytoskeleton comprises microfilaments (actin), intermediate filaments, and microtubules (tubulin) orchestrating cellular mechanics, shape maintenance, and motility.
Regarding ciliary axoneme organization: Eukaryotic cilia and flagella possess an axonemal core with nine peripheral microtubule doublets radially linked to a central pair of tubules (9 + 2 arrangement).
Regarding centriolar ultrastructure: Centrioles do not possess a 9 + 2 doublet arrangement; instead, they display a cartwheel layout composed of nine peripheral triplets of tubulin (9 + 0 array) devoid of central microtubules.
Regarding the centriolar hub: The central proximal part of the centriole forms a proteinaceous cylinder called the hub, from which nine radial spokes extend to link the peripheral triplets.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The assertions regarding the cytoskeleton, the 9+2 axonemal array of cilia, and the centriolar hub are correct, while the assertion asserting identical doublet architecture in centrioles is incorrect. Therefore, only the first, second, and fourth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
यूकैरियोटिक कोशिका कंकाल संरचनात्मक दृढ़ता और गति प्रदान करता है, जिसमें ट्यूबुलिन संयोजन या तो 9+2 युग्मकों (पक्ष्माभ/कशाभ) या 9+0 त्रिकों (तारककेंद्र) के रूप में व्यवस्थित होते हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
कोशिका कंकाल के घटकों का मूल्यांकन: कोशिका कंकाल में सूक्ष्मनलिकाएं, सूक्ष्मप्रतंतु और मध्यवर्ती तंतु होते हैं जो यांत्रिक सहारा, कोशिका का आकार और गतिशीलता प्रदान करते हैं।
पक्ष्माभ अक्षसूत्र का मूल्यांकन: पक्ष्माभ और यूकैरियोटिक कशाभ के अक्षसूत्र में परिधि पर नौ युग्मक और केंद्र में दो एकल नलिकाएं (9 + 2 विन्यास) पाई जाती हैं।
तारककेंद्र की परासंरचना का मूल्यांकन: तारककेंद्र में 9 + 2 युग्मक विन्यास नहीं होता; इसमें गाड़ी के पहिए जैसा 9 + 0 विन्यास होता है जिसमें परिधि पर नौ त्रिक (ट्रिपलेट्स) होते हैं और केंद्र में नलिकाएं नहीं होतीं। अतः तीसरा कथन गलत है।
तारककेंद्र की धुरी (हब) का मूल्यांकन: तारककेंद्र का मध्य भाग प्रोटीनयुक्त धुरी (हब) कहलाता है, जो अरीय दंडों द्वारा परिधीय त्रिकों से जुड़ा रहता है।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय और चतुर्थ प्रतिपादन सत्य हैं, जबकि तृतीय प्रतिपादन असत्य है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय और चतुर्थ प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

answer.text: I, II, III and IV are correct
I, II and III only are correct
I, II and IV only are correct
II and IV only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q08 - Interphase chromatin composition nuclear pores and chromosome classification

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: Chromatin of the interphase nucleus contains DNA, basic proteins called histones, non-histone proteins, and RNA.

Statement II: Nuclear pores are formed by the fusion of the two nuclear membranes, providing bidirectional transit passages for RNA and proteins between nucleus and cytoplasm.

Statement III: Based on the position of the centromere, a metacentric chromosome has a middle centromere forming two equal arms.

Statement IV: An acrocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere located at the extreme tip of the chromosome.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अंतरावस्था केंद्रक के क्रोमैटिन में डीएनए, हिस्टोन नामक क्षारीय प्रोटीन, गैर-हिस्टोन प्रोटीन और आरएनए पाए जाते हैं।

कथन II: केंद्रक छिद्र दोनों केंद्रक झिल्लियों के संलयन से बनते हैं, जो केंद्रक और कोशिकाद्रव्य के बीच आरएनए और प्रोटीनों के द्विदिशीय परिवहन मार्ग प्रदान करते हैं।

कथन III: गुणसूत्रबिंदु (सेंट्रोमियर) की स्थिति के आधार पर, मध्यकेंद्री (मेटासेंट्रिक) गुणसूत्र में सेंट्रोमियर मध्य में होता है जिससे दो समान भुजाएं बनती हैं।

कथन IV: अग्रकेंद्री (एक्रोसेंट्रिक) गुणसूत्र में गुणसूत्रबिंदु गुणसूत्र के अंतिम सिरे पर स्थित होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The eukaryotic nucleus encloses chromatin fibers and facilitates nucleocytoplasmic transport via nuclear pores, with chromosomes categorized by the position of their primary constriction (centromere).

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding chromatin biochemical composition: Nucleoprotein fibers of interphase chromatin consist of DNA, basic histone proteins, non-histone chromosomal proteins, and small amounts of RNA.
Regarding nuclear pores: The nuclear envelope is interrupted by nuclear pore complexes formed by the fusion of inner and outer nuclear membranes, regulating bidirectional traffic of ribonucleoproteins, mRNA, and regulatory factors.
Regarding metacentric morphology: A metacentric chromosome possesses a centrally located centromere, yielding two morphological arms of equal length.
Regarding acrocentric versus telocentric classification: An acrocentric chromosome has its centromere located close to one end, yielding one extremely short and one very long arm. A terminal centromere located at the extreme tip defines a telocentric chromosome. The fourth assertion erroneously assigns telocentric morphology to an acrocentric chromosome.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The statements on chromatin composition, nuclear pore function, and metacentric chromosomes are correct, while the definition of an acrocentric chromosome is incorrect. Therefore, only the first, second, and third propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
यूकैरियोटिक केंद्रक क्रोमैटिन तंतुओं को समाहित करता है और केंद्रक छिद्रों द्वारा परिवहन संचालित करता है; गुणसूत्रों को उनके गुणसूत्रबिंदु की स्थिति के आधार पर वर्गीकृत किया जाता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
क्रोमैटिन के रासायनिक संघटन का मूल्यांकन: अंतरावस्था केंद्रक के क्रोमैटिन जाल में डीएनए, क्षारीय हिस्टोन प्रोटीन, गैर-हिस्टोन प्रोटीन और आरएनए उपस्थित होते हैं।
केंद्रक छिद्रों के कार्य का मूल्यांकन: आंतरिक और बाहरी केंद्रक झिल्ली के संलयन से बनने वाले केंद्रक छिद्र केंद्रक और कोशिकाद्रव्य के मध्य आरएनए और प्रोटीन अणुओं के आवागमन के लिए द्विदिशीय मार्ग प्रदान करते हैं।
मेटासेंट्रिक गुणसूत्र का मूल्यांकन: मेटासेंट्रिक गुणसूत्र में सेंट्रोमियर बिल्कुल मध्य में स्थित होता है, जिससे गुणसूत्र की दोनों भुजाएं समान लंबाई की बनती हैं।
एक्रोसेंट्रिक बनाम टेलोसेंट्रिक गुणसूत्र का मूल्यांकन: अग्रकेंद्री (एक्रोसेंट्रिक) गुणसूत्र में सेंट्रोमियर सिरे के निकट होता है (एक अत्यंत छोटी और एक बहुत लंबी भुजा), जबकि सिरे पर स्थित (टर्मिनल) सेंट्रोमियर अंत्यकेंद्री (टेलोसेंट्रिक) गुणसूत्र का लक्षण है। अतः चतुर्थ कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय और तृतीय प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि चतुर्थ प्रतिपादन गलत है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय और तृतीय प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q01 - Prokaryotic cellular organization morphology and inclusions

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding prokaryotic cells:

Statement I: Prokaryotes are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma, and PPLO.

Statement II: The four basic shapes of bacteria are bacillus, coccus, vibrio, and spirillum.

Statement III: All prokaryotes without any exception possess a rigid peptidoglycan cell wall.

Statement IV: Inclusion bodies in prokaryotes are non-membrane bound and lie free in the cytoplasm.

Statement V: Bacterial flagellum consists of filament, hook, and basal body.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं के संदर्भ में नीचे पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: प्रोकैरियोट्स का प्रतिनिधित्व जीवाणु, नीले-हरे शैवाल, माइकोप्लाज्मा और PPLO द्वारा किया जाता है।

कथन II: जीवाणुओं के चार मूलभूत आकार बैसिलस, कोकस, विब्रियो और स्पाइरिलम होते हैं।

कथन III: बिना किसी अपवाद के सभी प्रोकैरियोट्स में एक कठोर पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन कोशिका भित्ति होती है।

कथन IV: प्रोकैरियोट्स में अंतर्विष्ट पिंड (इन्क्लूजन बॉडीज) झिल्ली-रहित होते हैं और कोशिकाद्रव्य में स्वतंत्र रूप से पड़े रहते हैं।

कथन V: जीवाणु कशाभिका तंतु, अंकुश और आधारी काय से मिलकर बनती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prokaryotic organisms share fundamental structural features such as lack of membrane-bound organelles, presence of 70S ribosomes, diverse cell envelopes, and non-membrane-bound cytoplasmic reserves.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding representative organisms: Prokaryotes include eubacteria, cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), mycoplasmas, and PPLO (pleuropneumonia-like organisms).
Regarding bacterial morphology: The four canonical bacterial morphological types are rod-shaped bacillus, spherical coccus, comma-shaped vibrio, and spiral spirillum.
Regarding the cell wall exception: Although most prokaryotes possess a cell wall surrounding the plasma membrane, Mycoplasmas are a notable exception as they completely lack a cell wall.
Regarding inclusion bodies: Prokaryotic nutrient reserves (such as phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, and glycogen granules) are stored as non-membrane-bound inclusion bodies lying freely in the cytosol.
Regarding flagellar structure: Motile bacteria possess flagella composed of an elongated filament, a curved hook, and an anchoring basal body.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The assertions concerning representative taxa, morphological shapes, inclusion bodies, and flagellar anatomy are factually accurate, while the claim that all prokaryotes without exception have a cell wall is inaccurate. Therefore, only the first, second, fourth, and fifth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
प्रोकैरियोटिक जीवों में झिल्ली-युक्त अंगकों का अभाव, नग्न आनुवंशिक पदार्थ और विशिष्ट कोशिका आवरण जैसी मूलभूत समानताएं पाई जाती हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
प्रतिनिधि जीवों का मूल्यांकन: प्रोकैरियोट्स के अंतर्गत जीवाणु, नीले-हरे शैवाल, माइकोप्लाज्मा और PPLO शामिल हैं।
जीवाणु आकारों का मूल्यांकन: जीवाणुओं के चार मूलभूत आकार दंडाकार (बैसिलस), गोलाकार (कोकस), कॉमा के आकार के (विब्रियो) और सर्पिलाकार (स्पाइरिलम) होते हैं।
कोशिका भित्ति के अपवाद का मूल्यांकन: यद्यपि अधिकांश प्रोकैरियोट्स में कोशिका भित्ति पाई जाती है, किंतु माइकोप्लाज्मा में कोशिका भित्ति पूर्णतः अनुपस्थित होती है। अतः बिना किसी अपवाद के सभी में भित्ति बताना गलत है।
अंतर्विष्ट पिंडों का मूल्यांकन: प्रोकैरियोटिक आरक्षित पदार्थ (फॉस्फेट कण, सायनोफाइसियन कण, ग्लाइकोजन कण) किसी झिल्ली से घिरे नहीं होते और कोशिकाद्रव्य में स्वतंत्र रहते हैं।
कशाभिका की संरचना का मूल्यांकन: जीवाणु कशाभ तीन भागों—तंतु (फिलामेंट), अंकुश (हुक) और आधारी काय (बेसल बॉडी) से मिलकर बना होता है।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय, चतुर्थ और पंचम प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि तृतीय प्रतिपादन असत्य है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, चतुर्थ और पंचम प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

answer.text: I, II, IV and V only are correct
I, II, III and IV only are correct
II, III, IV and V only are correct
I, II, III, IV and V are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q02 - Biochemical constituents and dynamics of biological membranes

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding biological membranes:

Statement I: Membrane lipids are primarily phospholipids arranged in a continuous bilayer.

Statement II: The polar head of the phospholipid bilayer faces inward toward the hydrophobic core.

Statement III: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model of cell membrane in 1972.

Statement IV: The quasi-fluid nature of lipids enables the lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

Statement V: Polar molecules require carrier proteins to facilitate their passage across the nonpolar lipid interior.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

जैविक झिल्लियों के संदर्भ में नीचे पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: झिल्ली के लिपिड मुख्य रूप से फॉस्फोलिपिड होते हैं जो एक सतत द्विसतह में व्यवस्थित होते हैं।

कथन II: फॉस्फोलिपिड द्विसतह के ध्रुवीय शीर्ष जल-विरोधी आंतरिक कोर की ओर अंदर की तरफ उन्मुख होते हैं।

कथन III: सिंगर और निकोलसन ने 1972 में कोशिका झिल्ली का तरल मोज़ेक मॉडल प्रस्तुत किया था।

कथन IV: लिपिड की अर्ध-तरल प्रकृति द्विसतह के भीतर प्रोटीनों के पार्श्व संचलन को सुगम बनाती है।

कथन V: ध्रुवीय अणुओं को अध्रुवीय लिपिड आंतरिक भाग से गुजरने के लिए वाहक प्रोटीनों की आवश्यकता होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The fluid mosaic model explains plasma membrane organization as an amphipathic lipid bilayer that provides a viscous fluid matrix within which proteins can move laterally, regulating selective transport.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding phospholipid bilayer arrangement: Phospholipids are the principal structural lipids of biomembranes, assembled into a double layer.
Regarding polar head orientation: The hydrophilic polar heads are oriented outward toward the aqueous cytosolic and extracellular environments, while the hydrophobic nonpolar hydrocarbon tails are sheltered internally. The second assertion describes the reverse orientation.
Regarding the fluid mosaic milestone: Singer and Nicolson formulated the widely accepted fluid mosaic model in 1972.
Regarding membrane fluidity and protein movement: The quasi-fluidity of the membrane bilayer enables the lateral displacement of proteins, which defines membrane fluidity.
Regarding polar solute transport: Because polar molecules cannot freely traverse the hydrophobic core of the bilayer, their transport is mediated by specialized transmembrane carrier proteins.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The statements on phospholipid bilayer identity, the 1972 model, lateral mobility, and facilitated transport of polar solutes are accurate, whereas the statement claiming inward-facing polar heads is incorrect. Therefore, only the first, third, fourth, and fifth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
तरल मोज़ेक मॉडल के अनुसार कोशिका झिल्ली एक उभयसंवेदी लिपिड द्विसतह है जो अर्ध-तरल माध्यम प्रदान करती है, जिसमें प्रोटीन पार्श्व गति कर सकते हैं और चयनात्मक पारगमन को नियंत्रित करते हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
फॉस्फोलिपिड द्विसतह का मूल्यांकन: जैविक झिल्लियों का मुख्य संरचनात्मक घटक फॉस्फोलिपिड होते हैं जो द्विसतह के रूप में व्यवस्थित रहते हैं।
ध्रुवीय शीर्षों के विन्यास का मूल्यांकन: फॉस्फोलिपिड के ध्रुवीय जल-स्नेही शीर्ष बाहर की ओर जलीय माध्यम के संपर्क में रहते हैं, जबकि अध्रुवीय पूंछ अंदर की ओर सुरक्षित रहती है। अतः ध्रुवीय शीर्षों को अंदर की ओर बताना गलत है।
तरल मोज़ेक मॉडल के इतिहास का मूल्यांकन: एस.जे. सिंगर और जी.एल. निकोलसन ने 1972 में तरल मोज़ेक मॉडल प्रतिपादित किया था।
प्रोटीन पार्श्व गति का मूल्यांकन: लिपिड की अर्ध-तरल प्रकृति द्विसतह के भीतर प्रोटीनों के पार्श्व संचलन को संभव बनाती है, जिसे झिल्ली की तरलता कहा जाता है।
ध्रुवीय अणुओं के परिवहन का मूल्यांकन: ध्रुवीय अणु अध्रुवीय लिपिड कोर को पार नहीं कर सकते, इसलिए उन्हें झिल्ली के पार जाने के लिए विशिष्ट वाहक प्रोटीन की आवश्यकता होती है।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, तृतीय, चतुर्थ और पंचम प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि द्वितीय प्रतिपादन असत्य है। अतः केवल प्रथम, तृतीय, चतुर्थ और पंचम प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q03 - Endomembrane coordination ER Golgi lysosomes and vacuoles

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding the eukaryotic endomembrane system:

Statement I: The endomembrane system comprises the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles.

Statement II: Rough endoplasmic reticulum bears ribosomes on its outer surface and is actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion.

Statement III: In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesized in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

Statement IV: Proteins synthesized by ribosomes enter the Golgi apparatus directly through its concave trans face.

Statement V: In plant cells, the tonoplast actively transports ions against concentration gradients into the vacuole.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

यूकैरियोटिक अंतःझिल्ली तंत्र के संदर्भ में नीचे पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अंतःझिल्ली तंत्र के अंतर्गत अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका (ER), गॉल्जी संकुल, लयनकाय (लाइसोसोम) और रसधानियां शामिल हैं।

कथन II: खुरदरी अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका (RER) की बाहरी सतह पर राइबोसोम उपस्थित होते हैं और यह प्रोटीन संश्लेषण व स्राव में सक्रिय रूप से भाग लेती है।

कथन III: जंतु कोशिकाओं में लिपिड सदृश स्टेरॉयड हार्मोन चिकनी अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका (SER) में संश्लेषित होते हैं।

कथन IV: राइबोसोम द्वारा संश्लेषित प्रोटीन गॉल्जी उपकरण में सीधे उसकी अवतल ट्रांस सतह के माध्यम से प्रवेश करते हैं।

कथन V: पादप कोशिकाओं में टोनोप्लास्ट सांद्रता प्रवणता के विपरीत कई आयनों के रसधानी में परिवहन को सुगम बनाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The endomembrane system functions as an integrated pipeline for polypeptide synthesis, lipid production, vesicular trafficking, glycosylation, and lysosomal/vacuolar delivery.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding system constituents: The endomembrane system is defined by functional interdependence and includes the ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles.
Regarding RER functions: RER is studded with ribosomes on its cytosolic surface and synthesizes secretory and membrane-associated proteins.
Regarding SER functions: SER lacks ribosomes and synthesizes lipids, phospholipids, and steroid hormones.
Regarding Golgi polarity and entry: Vesicles budding from the ER fuse with the convex cis face (forming face) of the Golgi cisternae, undergo processing, and exit via the concave trans face (maturing face). Stating that proteins enter through the trans face is incorrect.
Regarding tonoplast active transport: In plants, the tonoplast membrane maintains significantly higher solute concentrations inside the vacuolar sap by pumping ions against steep concentration gradients.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The assertions regarding the components of the endomembrane system, RER synthesis, SER steroidogenesis, and vacuolar tonoplast transport are accurate, whereas the statement specifying the trans face as the vesicle entry point is inaccurate. Therefore, only the first, second, third, and fifth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
अंतःझिल्ली तंत्र एक समन्वित तंत्र है जो प्रोटीन और लिपिड संश्लेषण, रूपांतरण, संवेष्टन और रसधानी परिवहन को संचालित करता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
घटकों का मूल्यांकन: अंतःझिल्ली तंत्र में ER, गॉल्जी उपकरण, लयनकाय और रसधानियां शामिल हैं क्योंकि इनके कार्य परस्पर जुड़े होते हैं।
RER के कार्यों का मूल्यांकन: खुरदरी अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका की सतह पर राइबोसोम पाए जाते हैं और यह प्रोटीन निर्माण व स्राव का प्रमुख स्थल है।
SER के कार्यों का मूल्यांकन: चिकनी अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका लिपिड और जंतुओं में स्टेरॉयड हार्मोनों के संश्लेषण के लिए समर्पित होती है।
गॉल्जी में प्रवेश की दिशा का मूल्यांकन: ER से आने वाले प्रोटीन पुटिकाओं के रूप में गॉल्जी की उत्तल सिस (निर्माणकारी) सतह से संलयित होकर प्रवेश करते हैं, न कि अवतल ट्रांस सतह से। अतः चौथा कथन गलत है।
टोनोप्लास्ट के कार्य का मूल्यांकन: पादप रसधानी की झिल्ली (टोनोप्लास्ट) आयनों को सांद्रता प्रवणता के विपरीत सक्रिय रूप से रसधानी के भीतर ले जाती है।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और पंचम प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि चतुर्थ प्रतिपादन गलत है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और पंचम प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

answer.text: I, II, III and IV only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q04 - Mitochondria and chloroplast ultrastructure and genetic autonomy

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding mitochondria and chloroplasts:

Statement I: Both mitochondria and chloroplasts are double membrane-bound organelles.

Statement II: Mitochondria are the primary sites of aerobic cellular respiration and ATP generation.

Statement III: The inner membrane of chloroplasts forms extensive infoldings called cristae that project into the stroma.

Statement IV: The matrix of mitochondria and the stroma of chloroplasts both contain small circular DNA molecules.

Statement V: The ribosomes present inside both mitochondria and chloroplasts are of the 70S type.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और हरितलवक (क्लोरोप्लास्ट) के संदर्भ में नीचे पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और हरितलवक दोनों ही दोहरी झिल्ली-युक्त अंगक हैं।

कथन II: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया वायवीय कोशिकीय श्वसन और एटीपी उत्पादन के मुख्य स्थल हैं।

कथन III: हरितलवक की आंतरिक झिल्ली व्यापक अंतर्वलन बनाती है जिन्हें क्रिस्टी कहते हैं, जो स्ट्रोमा में प्रक्षिप्त होते हैं।

कथन IV: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया की आधात्री और हरितलवक के स्ट्रोमा दोनों में छोटे वृत्ताकार डीएनए अणु पाए जाते हैं।

कथन V: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और हरितलवक दोनों के भीतर उपस्थित राइबोसोम 70S प्रकार के होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous double-membrane organelles that evolved via endosymbiosis, retaining circular DNA genomes, prokaryotic 70S ribosomes, and specialized bioenergetic membranes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding double-membrane organization: Both organelles are bounded by distinct outer and inner lipid membranes.
Regarding mitochondrial energy transduction: Mitochondria house the enzymes of the tricarboxylic acid cycle and respiratory chain, serving as cellular power plants generating ATP via aerobic respiration.
Regarding cristae location: Cristae are infoldings formed specifically by the inner membrane of mitochondria to expand respiratory surface area; in chloroplasts, the inner membrane encloses the stroma, within which thylakoids form grana rather than cristae.
Regarding organellar genomes: Both the mitochondrial matrix and the chloroplast stroma possess small, naked, circular double-stranded DNA molecules.
Regarding organellar ribosomes: Both organelles contain 70S ribosomes distinct from the 80S ribosomes present in eukaryotic cytosol.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The statements on double-membrane architecture, mitochondrial ATP synthesis, organellar circular DNA, and 70S ribosomes are accurate, whereas the statement attributing cristae to chloroplasts is inaccurate. Therefore, only the first, second, fourth, and fifth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और हरितलवक अर्ध-स्वायत्त दोहरी झिल्ली वाले अंगक हैं, जिनमें वृत्ताकार डीएनए, 70S राइबोसोम और विशिष्ट ऊर्जा रूपांतरण प्रणालियां उपस्थित होती हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
दोहरी झिल्ली का मूल्यांकन: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और हरितलवक दोनों दोहरी झिल्ली से घिरे अंगक हैं।
माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया में श्वसन का मूल्यांकन: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया वायवीय श्वसन के मुख्य स्थल हैं जहां ऑक्सीडेटिव फॉस्फोराइलेशन द्वारा एटीपी का निर्माण होता है।
क्रिस्टी की उपस्थिति का मूल्यांकन: क्रिस्टी माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया की भीतरी झिल्ली के अंतर्वलन होते हैं, हरितलवक के नहीं। हरितलवक के स्ट्रोमा में थायलाकोइड पाए जाते हैं। अतः तीसरा कथन असत्य है।
अंगकीय डीएनए का मूल्यांकन: माइटोकॉन्ड्रियल मैट्रिक्स और क्लोरोप्लास्ट स्ट्रोमा दोनों में वृत्ताकार डीएनए अणु उपस्थित होते हैं।
अंगकीय राइबोसोम का मूल्यांकन: इन दोनों अंगकों के आंतरिक भाग में उपस्थित राइबोसोम 70S प्रकार के होते हैं।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय, चतुर्थ और पंचम प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि तृतीय प्रतिपादन असत्य है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, चतुर्थ और पंचम प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q05 - Ultrastructural features of eukaryotic cilia flagella and centrioles

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding cilia, flagella, and centrosomes:

Statement I: The core of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum is called the axoneme and is covered by the plasma membrane.

Statement II: The axoneme exhibits a 9 + 2 array of microtubules consisting of nine peripheral doublets and a centrally located pair of singlet microtubules.

Statement III: Nine radial spokes connect the central sheath to one tubule of each peripheral doublet in the axoneme.

Statement IV: Centrioles have an internal axoneme identical to cilia, containing nine peripheral doublets and two central singlet tubules.

Statement V: Centrioles serve as the basal bodies from which cilia and flagella emerge.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

पक्ष्माभ (सिलिया), कशाभ (फ्लैजिला) और तारककाय (सेंट्रोसोम) के संदर्भ में नीचे पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: यूकैरियोटिक पक्ष्माभ या कशाभ के आंतरिक कोर को अक्षसूत्र (एक्सोनीम) कहा जाता है और यह प्लाज्मा झिल्ली से ढका होता है।

कथन II: अक्षसूत्र में सूक्ष्मनलिकाओं का 9 + 2 विन्यास होता है जिसमें नौ परिधीय युग्मक (डबलेट्स) और केंद्र में एक जोड़ी एकल सूक्ष्मनलिकाएं होती हैं।

कथन III: अक्षसूत्र में नौ अरीय दंड (रेडियल स्पोक्स) केंद्रीय आवरण को प्रत्येक परिधीय युग्मक की एक नलिका से जोड़ते हैं।

कथन IV: तारककेंद्रों (सेंट्रिओल्स) का आंतरिक अक्षसूत्र सिलिया के बिल्कुल समान होता है, जिसमें नौ परिधीय युग्मक और दो केंद्रीय एकल नलिकाएं पाई जाती हैं।

कथन V: तारककेंद्र आधारी काय (बेसल बॉडी) का निर्माण करते हैं जिससे पक्ष्माभ और कशाभ निकलते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Motility and division apparatus in eukaryotic cells rely on tubulin-based cytoskeletal cylinders that assemble into either axonemal 9+2 doublets (cilia and flagella) or triplet-based cartwheel structures (centrioles and basal bodies).

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding axoneme identity and sheath: The axoneme forms the central structural axis of cilia and flagella, completely enveloped by the plasma membrane.
Regarding the 9 + 2 array: Longitudinal microtubule doublets form a peripheral ring of nine, encircling two central singlet microtubules connected by bridges.
Regarding radial spokes: Nine proteinaceous radial spokes project inward from each peripheral doublet to attach to the central sheath surrounding the central singlet tubules.
Regarding centriolar ultrastructure: Centrioles do not possess a 9 + 2 doublet array; they are composed of nine peripheral triplets of microtubules arranged in a cartwheel pattern (9 + 0 array) lacking central microtubules.
Regarding basal body function: Centrioles form basal bodies from which cilia and eukaryotic flagella originate, and they organize mitotic spindle fibers in animal cells.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The statements detailing ciliary axonemal anatomy, the 9+2 configuration, radial spoke linkages, and basal body derivation are correct, while the statement claiming identical doublet architecture in centrioles is incorrect. Therefore, only the first, second, third, and fifth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
यूकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में गति और कोशिका विभाजन ट्यूबुलिन प्रोटीन से निर्मित विशिष्ट संरचनाओं पर निर्भर करते हैं, जो 9+2 युग्मकों (पक्ष्माभ/कशाभ) अथवा 9+0 त्रिकों (तारककेंद्र/आधारी काय) के रूप में व्यवस्थित होते हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
अक्षसूत्र के आवरण का मूल्यांकन: पक्ष्माभ और कशाभ का मुख्य आंतरिक भाग अक्षसूत्र (एक्सोनीम) कहलाता है, जो प्लाज्मा झिल्ली से ढका रहता है।
9 + 2 विन्यास का मूल्यांकन: अक्षसूत्र में परिधि पर नौ युग्मक (डबलेट्स) और केंद्र में दो एकल नलिकाएं होती हैं, जिसे 9 + 2 विन्यास कहा जाता है।
अरीय दंडों (रेडियल स्पोक्स) का मूल्यांकन: केंद्रीय आवरण से परिधि के प्रत्येक युग्मक की एक नलिका तक नौ अरीय दंड फैले होते हैं।
तारककेंद्र की परासंरचना का मूल्यांकन: तारककेंद्र में 9 + 2 युग्मक विन्यास नहीं होता; इसमें परिधि पर नौ त्रिक (ट्रिपलेट्स) होते हैं तथा केंद्र में नलिकाएं नहीं होतीं (9 + 0 विन्यास)। अतः चौथा कथन गलत है।
आधारी काय के निर्माण का मूल्यांकन: तारककेंद्र पक्ष्माभ और कशाभ के आधारी काय (बेसल बॉडी) का निर्माण करते हैं जहां से ये चलन अंगक निकलते हैं।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और पंचम प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि चतुर्थ प्रतिपादन गलत है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और पंचम प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_STATEMENTBASED_Q06 - Nuclear envelope architecture chromatin constitution and chromosomal types

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding the eukaryotic nucleus and chromosomes:

Statement I: The nuclear envelope consists of two parallel membranes separated by a perinuclear space of 10 to 50 nm.

Statement II: The outer nuclear membrane is continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and bears ribosomes on its cytoplasmic face.

Statement III: The nucleolus is a non-membrane bound sub-nuclear structure that serves as the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

Statement IV: A sub-metacentric chromosome possesses a centromere positioned extremely close to one end, resulting in one extremely short arm and one very long arm.

Statement V: Secondary constrictions present on certain chromosomes demarcate a terminal chromosomal fragment termed a satellite.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

यूकैरियोटिक केंद्रक और गुणसूत्रों के संदर्भ में नीचे पांच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: केंद्रक आवरण में दो समानांतर झिल्लियां होती हैं जिनके बीच 10 से 50 nm का परिकेंद्रकीय अवकाश होता है।

कथन II: बाहरी केंद्रक झिल्ली अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका (ER) के साथ निरंतर जुड़ी रहती है और इसकी कोशिकाद्रव्यी सतह पर राइबोसोम उपस्थित होते हैं।

कथन III: केंद्रिक (न्यूक्लियोलस) एक झिल्ली-रहित संरचना है जो सक्रिय राइबोसोमल आरएनए (rRNA) संश्लेषण के स्थल के रूप में कार्य करती है।

कथन IV: एक उप-मध्यकेंद्री (सब-मेटासेंट्रिक) गुणसूत्र में गुणसूत्रबिंदु एक सिरे के बहुत निकट स्थित होता है, जिससे एक अत्यंत छोटी भुजा और एक बहुत लंबी भुजा बनती है।

कथन V: कुछ गुणसूत्रों पर उपस्थित द्वितीयक संकीर्णन एक छोटे अग्रस्थ गुणसूत्रीय खंड को सीमांकित करते हैं जिसे उपग्रह (सैटेलाइट) कहा जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The eukaryotic nucleus contains a double-membrane envelope interrupted by pores, non-membrane-bound nucleolar compartments, and chromatin organized into chromosomes classified by centromeric locus.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertions
Regarding the nuclear envelope and perinuclear space: The nuclear envelope comprises inner and outer lipid bilayers separated by a 10 to 50 nm perinuclear space acting as a molecular boundary.
Regarding outer membrane connectivity: The outer nuclear membrane is confluent with the rough endoplasmic reticulum and studded with ribosomes.
Regarding nucleolar architecture: The nucleolus is not delimited by a membrane and is directly bathed in nucleoplasm; it represents the transcription and assembly hub for ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
Regarding chromosome morphology: A sub-metacentric chromosome has its centromere situated slightly away from the center, yielding one slightly shorter arm and one slightly longer arm. In contrast, an acrocentric chromosome has its centromere located close to one end, producing one extremely short and one very long arm. The fourth assertion erroneously assigns acrocentric morphology to a sub-metacentric chromosome.
Regarding satellites: Some chromosomes possess non-staining secondary constrictions at defined positions that set off a small terminal knob-like segment termed a satellite.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The statements describing the perinuclear envelope, outer membrane continuity, nucleolar rRNA synthesis, and chromosomal satellites are correct, while the statement defining sub-metacentric chromosome arm ratio is incorrect. Therefore, only the first, second, third, and fifth propositions are correct.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
यूकैरियोटिक केंद्रक में दोहरी झिल्ली वाला छिद्रयुक्त आवरण, झिल्ली-रहित केंद्रिक और गुणसूत्रबिंदु की स्थिति के अनुसार वर्गीकृत गुणसूत्र पाए जाते हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
परिकेंद्रकीय अवकाश का मूल्यांकन: केंद्रक आवरण दो समानांतर झिल्लियों से बना होता है जिनके बीच 10 से 50 nm का परिकेंद्रकीय अवकाश होता है।
बाहरी झिल्ली के जुड़ाव का मूल्यांकन: बाहरी केंद्रक झिल्ली खुरदरी अंतःद्रव्यी जालिका के साथ निरंतर जुड़ी होती है और इसकी सतह पर राइबोसोम पाए जाते हैं।
केंद्रिक (न्यूक्लियोलस) के कार्य का मूल्यांकन: केंद्रिक झिल्ली-रहित संरचना है जो केंद्रकद्रव्य के सीधे संपर्क में रहती है तथा सक्रिय राइबोसोमल आरएनए (rRNA) संश्लेषण का प्रमुख स्थल है।
सब-मेटासेंट्रिक गुणसूत्र का मूल्यांकन: सब-मेटासेंट्रिक गुणसूत्र में सेंट्रोमियर मध्य से थोड़ा हटकर होता है जिससे एक भुजा थोड़ी छोटी और एक भुजा थोड़ी लंबी होती है। एक सिरे के बहुत निकट सेंट्रोमियर होना (अत्यंत छोटी और बहुत लंबी भुजा) अग्रकेंद्री (एक्रोसेंट्रिक) गुणसूत्र का लक्षण है। अतः चौथा कथन गलत है।
द्वितीयक संकीर्णन और सैटेलाइट का मूल्यांकन: कुछ गुणसूत्रों में निश्चित स्थानों पर गैर-अभिरंजित द्वितीयक संकीर्णन होते हैं जो सैटेलाइट (उपग्रह) कहलाने वाले छोटे खंड का निर्माण करते हैं।

चरण 3: परीक्षण एवं अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और पंचम प्रतिपादन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि चतुर्थ प्रतिपादन गलत है। अतः केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और पंचम प्रतिपादन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Discoveries and contributions of cell biologists

questiontext.text:
Match the scientists listed in Column I with their respective discoveries or contributions in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek I. Omnis cellula-e cellula
B. Robert Brown II. Fluid mosaic model of plasma membrane
C. Rudolf Virchow III. First saw and described a live cell
D. Singer and Nicolson IV. Discovery of the nucleus

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's contribution
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell using his improved microscope lenses.

Step 2: Identify Robert Brown's contribution
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831 as a distinct internal structure of the cell.

Step 3: Identify Rudolf Virchow's contribution
Rudolf Virchow in 1855 proposed the concept of Omnis cellula-e cellula, explaining that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Step 4: Identify Singer and Nicolson's contribution
Singer and Nicolson in 1972 proposed the fluid mosaic model, describing the structure and quasi-fluid dynamics of the plasma membrane.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek corresponds to first seeing and describing a live cell; Robert Brown corresponds to the discovery of the nucleus; Rudolf Virchow corresponds to Omnis cellula-e cellula; and Singer and Nicolson corresponds to the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Storage content of different leucoplast types

questiontext.text:
Match the plastids given in Column I with their stored reserve materials or functional pigments given in Column II:

Column I Column II

B. Elaioplast II. Stores carbohydrates such as starch
C. Aleuroplast III. Stores oils and fats
D. Chloroplast IV. Stores proteins

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the function of amyloplasts
Amyloplasts are non-pigmented leucoplasts specialised for the storage of carbohydrates, such as starch in potato tubers.

Step 2: Determine the function of elaioplasts
Elaioplasts are colourless leucoplasts that synthesise and store lipids, oils, and fats.

Step 3: Determine the function of aleuroplasts
Aleuroplasts are specialized leucoplasts that store nutrient proteins.

Step 4: Determine the function of chloroplasts
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments dedicated to trapping solar radiant energy for photosynthesis.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Amyloplast pairs with storage of carbohydrates such as starch; Elaioplast pairs with storage of oils and fats; Aleuroplast pairs with storage of proteins; and Chloroplast pairs with trapping light energy using chlorophyll and carotenoids.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Characteristic cell shapes across various cell types

questiontext.text:
Match the cell types listed in Column I with their characteristic shapes shown and described in the chapter in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Red blood cells I. Amoeboid
B. White blood cells II. Long and narrow
C. Columnar epithelial cells III. Round and biconcave
D. Mesophyll cells IV. Round and oval

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the shape of human red blood cells
Human erythrocytes are enucleated, round, and biconcave discs, approximately 7.0 µm in diameter, providing optimal surface area for gas exchange.

Step 2: Identify the shape of white blood cells
Leukocytes are amoeboid in shape, enabling diapedesis and pseudopodial movement through tissues.

Step 3: Identify the shape of columnar epithelial cells
Columnar epithelial cells are tall, pillar-like, long, and narrow structures with basally located nuclei.

Step 4: Identify the shape of mesophyll cells
Photosynthetic mesophyll cells of plant leaves are typically round and oval parenchymatous cells containing numerous chloroplasts.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Red blood cells match with round and biconcave; White blood cells match with amoeboid; Columnar epithelial cells match with long and narrow; and Mesophyll cells match with round and oval.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Surface and accessory structures of bacteria

questiontext.text:
Match the bacterial structures in Column I with their corresponding descriptions or roles in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Flagellum I. Small bristle-like fibres helping in attachment to rocks and host tissues
B. Pili II. Small circular DNA outside genomic DNA conferring antibiotic resistance
C. Fimbriae III. Filamentous organ composed of filament, hook, and basal body for motility
D. Plasmid IV. Elongated tubular structures made of a special protein

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize the bacterial flagellum
Bacterial flagella are filamentous extensions originating from the cell wall, composed of a basal body, hook, and filament, and serve specifically in cell motility.

Step 2: Characterize bacterial pili
Pili are elongated tubular appendages composed of specialized pilin protein; they do not mediate locomotion.

Step 3: Characterize bacterial fimbriae
Fimbriae are numerous small bristle-like protein fibres sprouting from the cell surface that facilitate attachment to substrates, stream rocks, and host tissues.

Step 4: Characterize bacterial plasmids
Plasmids are extrachromosomal, self-replicating, closed circular double-stranded DNA molecules that impart unique phenotypic advantages, such as antibiotic resistance.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Flagellum corresponds to the filamentous organ composed of filament, hook, and basal body for motility; Pili corresponds to elongated tubular structures made of a special protein; Fimbriae corresponds to small bristle-like fibres aiding attachment; and Plasmid corresponds to small circular extrachromosomal DNA conferring antibiotic resistance.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Endomembrane organelles and coordinate functions

questiontext.text:
Match the endomembrane organelles listed in Column I with their specific cellular functions in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum I. Digestion of macromolecules at acidic pH
B. Golgi apparatus II. Transport of ions against gradient in plant cells
C. Lysosomes III. Synthesis of lipids and steroidal hormones
D. Vacuolar tonoplast IV. Packaging and modification of glycoproteins and glycolipids

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER)
The SER lacks surface ribosomes and serves as the primary site for lipid biosynthesis, phospholipid formation, and synthesis of steroidal hormones in animal cells.

Step 2: Analyze the Golgi apparatus
The Golgi cisternae receive materials from the endoplasmic reticulum via transport vesicles, modify them, and act as key sites for assembling glycoproteins and glycolipids before secretion or sorting.

Step 3: Analyze lysosomes
Lysosomes are membrane-delimited vesicles rich in hydrolytic enzymes (such as lipases, proteases, carbohydrases, and nucleases) that function optimally under acidic pH to degrade macromolecules.

Step 4: Analyze the tonoplast of plant vacuoles
The tonoplast is the semi-permeable limiting membrane of the plant vacuole that facilitates active transport of ions against concentration gradients into the vacuolar sap.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum matches with synthesis of lipids and steroidal hormones; Golgi apparatus matches with packaging and modification of glycoproteins and glycolipids; Lysosomes match with digestion of macromolecules at acidic pH; and Vacuolar tonoplast matches with transport of ions against gradient in plant cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Centromere position and chromosome classification morphology

questiontext.text:
Match the chromosome types given in Column I with their centromeric positions and arm lengths in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Metacentric I. Terminal centromere at the tip of the chromosome
B. Sub-metacentric II. Centromere close to end forming one extremely short and one very long arm
C. Acrocentric III. Middle centromere forming two equal arms
D. Telocentric IV. Centromere slightly away from middle forming one shorter and one longer arm

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize metacentric chromosomes
Metacentric chromosomes possess a median centromere situated in the exact middle, producing two equal chromosome arms.

Step 2: Characterize sub-metacentric chromosomes
Sub-metacentric chromosomes possess a centromere displaced slightly away from the center, giving rise to one shorter arm (p arm) and one longer arm (q arm).

Step 3: Characterize acrocentric chromosomes
Acrocentric chromosomes have the centromere positioned sub-terminally very close to one end, yielding an extremely short arm and an unusually long arm.

Step 4: Characterize telocentric chromosomes
Telocentric chromosomes possess a strictly terminal centromere located at the extreme tip.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Metacentric matches with middle centromere forming two equal arms; Sub-metacentric matches with centromere slightly away from middle forming one shorter and one longer arm; Acrocentric matches with centromere close to end forming one extremely short and one very long arm; and Telocentric matches with terminal centromere at the tip.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Cytoskeletal and centriolar structural arrangements

questiontext.text:
Match the structural components of eukaryotic motility and cytoskeletal complexes in Column I with their organization patterns in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Ciliary axoneme I. Nine peripheral triplets linked to a central proteinaceous hub
B. Centriole II. Disc-shaped protein structures on the sides of the centromere
C. Basal body III. Nine doublets of peripheral microtubules and a central pair
D. Kinetochores IV. Centriole-like anchor structure from which cilia and flagella emerge

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the ciliary axoneme
The eukaryotic axoneme of cilia and flagella is composed of longitudinal microtubules organized into a classic \(9+2\) array: nine peripheral doublets encircling a central singlet pair.

Step 2: Evaluate the centriole
Centrioles display a cartwheel architecture consisting of nine evenly spaced peripheral triplets of tubulin fibrils connected via radial protein spokes to a central hub (\(9+0\) array).

Step 3: Evaluate the basal body
Basal bodies are centriole-derived structures positioned at the cell cortex that anchor cilia and eukaryotic flagella.

Step 4: Evaluate kinetochores
Kinetochores are specialized disc-shaped trilaminar protein plaques located on the lateral surfaces of chromosomal centromeres where spindle fibres attach during cell division.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Ciliary axoneme matches with nine doublets of peripheral microtubules and a central pair; Centriole matches with nine peripheral triplets linked to a central proteinaceous hub; Basal body matches with centriole-like anchor structure from which cilia and flagella emerge; and Kinetochores match with disc-shaped protein structures on the sides of the centromere.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Membrane transport mechanisms across plasma membrane

questiontext.text:
Match the transport processes across the plasma membrane in Column I with their fundamental mechanisms and characteristics in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Simple diffusion I. Energy-dependent movement of ions against concentration gradient using ATP
B. Osmosis II. Transport of polar molecules across nonpolar lipid bilayer via carrier proteins without energy
C. Facilitated transport III. Spontaneous passive flux of neutral solutes down their concentration gradient
D. Active transport IV. Passive diffusion of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate simple diffusion
Neutral solutes cross the hydrophobic phospholipid bilayer directly down their concentration gradient (from higher to lower concentration) without requiring carrier proteins or cellular energy expenditure.

Step 2: Evaluate osmosis
Osmosis is the net diffusion of water (solvent) across a selectively permeable membrane from an area of higher water concentration to lower water concentration.

Step 3: Evaluate facilitated transport
Because lipid bilayers are nonpolar and impermeable to polar molecules, polar solutes require membrane carrier proteins to facilitate their passage along the concentration gradient without ATP expenditure.

Step 4: Evaluate active transport
Active transport transports ions or molecules against their concentration gradient (from lower to higher concentration), consuming metabolic energy in the form of ATP, exemplified by the \(\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+\) ATPase pump.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Simple diffusion matches with spontaneous passive flux of neutral solutes down concentration gradient; Osmosis matches with passive diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane; Facilitated transport matches with transport of polar molecules across lipid bilayer via carrier proteins without energy; and Active transport matches with energy-dependent movement of ions against concentration gradient using ATP.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Specialized non-endomembrane compartments and inclusion structures

questiontext.text:

C. Nucleolus III. Membranous pigment-containing cytoplasmic extensions in cyanobacteria
D. Thylakoids IV. Non-membrane bound inclusion structures found in photosynthetic bacteria

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify gas vacuoles
Gas vacuoles are proteinaceous, non-unit-membrane-bound structures found in photosynthetic prokaryotes (blue-green, purple, and green photosynthetic bacteria) that provide buoyancy.

Step 2: Identify chromatophores
Chromatophores are specialized internal membranous extensions of the plasma membrane in cyanobacteria that harbor photosynthetic pigments.

Step 3: Identify the nucleolus
The nucleolus is a dense, non-membrane-delimited spherical region inside the nucleoplasm that acts as the primary site for the transcription and processing of precursor ribosomal RNA (rRNA).

Step 4: Identify thylakoids
Thylakoids are discrete, flattened membranous cisternae organized into stacks (grana) within the stroma of chloroplasts, housing chlorophyll pigments for photosynthetic light reactions.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Gas vacuoles correspond to non-membrane bound inclusion structures found in photosynthetic bacteria; Chromatophores correspond to membranous pigment-containing cytoplasmic extensions in cyanobacteria; Nucleolus corresponds to non-membrane bound site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis in the nucleoplasm; and Thylakoids correspond to flattened membranous sacs arranged in stacks in the chloroplast stroma.

questiontext.text:
Match the extracellular or envelope layers in Column I with their characteristic biochemical compositions or structural roles in Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Algal cell wall I. Calcium pectate layer that cements neighbouring plant cells together
B. Middle lamella II. Cellulose, galactans, mannans, and calcium carbonate
C. Plant cell wall III. Cytoplasmic channels traversing cell walls connecting adjacent cells
D. Plasmodesmata IV. Cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the composition of algal cell walls
The cell wall of algae exhibits a distinct composition containing cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals such as calcium carbonate.

Step 2: Determine the composition of the middle lamella
The middle lamella is an extracellular cementing layer predominantly composed of calcium pectate that binds adjacent plant cells together.

Step 3: Determine the composition of higher plant cell walls
Higher plant cell walls consist of cellulose microfibrils embedded in an amorphous matrix of hemicellulose, pectins, and structural proteins.

Step 4: Determine the role of plasmodesmata
Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels traversing the primary cell walls and middle lamellae, creating cytoplasmic continuity between adjoining plant cells.

Step 5: Final conceptual answer
Algal cell wall pairs with cellulose, galactans, mannans, and calcium carbonate; Middle lamella pairs with calcium pectate layer that cements neighbouring plant cells together; Plant cell wall pairs with cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins; and Plasmodesmata pairs with cytoplasmic channels traversing cell walls connecting adjacent cells.

answer.text: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Sequential pathway of protein secretion through endomembrane

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequential order representing the synthesis, processing, and intracellular trafficking of a secretory protein in a eukaryotic cell:

  1. Fusion of transport vesicles with the convex cis face of the Golgi apparatus
  2. Synthesis of the protein by ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum
  3. Release of processed proteins in vesicles from the concave trans face of the Golgi apparatus
  4. Modification of proteins within the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus
  5. Packaging of synthesised proteins into transport vesicles budding from the endoplasmic reticulum

Choose the correct sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the site of initial synthesis
Proteins destined for secretion or membrane targeting are translated by ribosomes attached to the outer surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) and enter the ER lumen.

Step 2: Trace transition from the endoplasmic reticulum
Synthesised proteins are packaged into transport vesicles that bud off from the endoplasmic reticulum for transit to the Golgi apparatus.

Step 3: Track entry into the Golgi complex
These ER-derived vesicles migrate and fuse with the convex cis (forming) face of the Golgi apparatus, delivering their contents into the organelle's lumen.

Step 4: Trace transit through cisternae for chemical modification
Proteins move through the stacked cisternae from the forming face towards the maturing face, where post-translational modifications (such as glycosylation into glycoproteins) occur.

Step 5: Identify the terminal exit from the Golgi apparatus
Modified and sorted proteins are packaged into secretory vesicles and bud off from the concave trans (maturing) face of the Golgi apparatus to be delivered to intracellular targets or secreted across the plasma membrane.

Step 6: Final conceptual answer
The correct functional sequence is: Synthesis of the protein on the rough endoplasmic reticulum → Packaging into transport vesicles budding from the ER → Fusion of vesicles with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus → Modification of proteins within the Golgi cisternae → Release of vesicles from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus (II → V → I → IV → III).

answer.text: II → V → I → IV → III
II → I → V → IV → III
V → II → I → III → IV
II → V → IV → I → III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological order of foundational discoveries in cell biology

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following historical milestones and discoveries in cell biology in the correct chronological order:

  1. Discovery and description of the cell nucleus by Robert Brown
  2. Proposal of the Fluid Mosaic Model of the plasma membrane by Singer and Nicolson
  3. First observation and description of a live cell by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
  4. Explanation that cells divide and new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula) by Rudolf Virchow
  5. First observation of densely stained reticular structures (Golgi bodies) near the nucleus by Camillo Golgi

Choose the correct chronological sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the earliest microscopic observation of a living cell
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first to see and describe a live cell using his improved simple microscope lenses during the late seventeenth century.

Step 2: Identify the discovery of the nucleus
Robert Brown discovered and described the nucleus as a distinct, constant organelle of the cell in 1831.

Step 3: Identify the formulation of cell origin
Rudolf Virchow in 1855 expanded and finalized the cell theory by demonstrating that cells divide and all new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).

Step 4: Identify the observation of the Golgi apparatus
Camillo Golgi in 1898 first identified and described the densely stained reticular network near the nucleus of nerve cells, later named Golgi bodies.

Step 5: Identify the modern membrane model
Singer and Nicolson proposed the widely accepted Fluid Mosaic Model of the cell membrane in 1972, explaining the bilayer structure and lateral fluidity of proteins.

Step 6: Final conceptual answer
The correct chronological order of discoveries is: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observing a live cell → Robert Brown discovering the nucleus (1831) → Rudolf Virchow formulating Omnis cellula-e cellula (1855) → Camillo Golgi observing Golgi bodies (1898) → Singer and Nicolson proposing the fluid mosaic model (1972) (III → I → IV → V → II).

answer.text: III → I → IV → V → II
III → IV → I → V → II
I → III → IV → V → II
III → I → V → IV → II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q01 - Discovery of the triple helical structure of collagen

questiontext.text: The triple helical structure of collagen was discovered and published in 1954 by which of the following scientists?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the historical contribution mentioned in the text
According to the introductory overview of Unit 3, G.N. Ramachandran was an outstanding figure in protein structure and the founder of the 'Madras school' of conformational analysis of biopolymers.

Step 2: Recall the specific structural discovery
His discovery of the triple helical structure of collagen was published in Nature in 1954, which remains a landmark contribution in structural biology.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the scientist who discovered the triple helical structure of collagen is G.N. Ramachandran.

answer.text: Linus Pauling
George Palade
Camillo Golgi
G.N. Ramachandran

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q02 - Significance of the Ramachandran plot in structural biology

questiontext.text: In structural biology, the 'Ramachandran plot' developed by G.N. Ramachandran is primarily used for:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the contribution of G.N. Ramachandran
G.N. Ramachandran made foundational contributions to structural biology through conformational analysis of biopolymers.

Step 2: Analyze the role of the Ramachandran plot
The Ramachandran plot was devised specifically to analyze and describe the stereochemically allowed conformations of polypeptide chains and proteins.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the Ramachandran plot is used for analyzing the allowed conformations of proteins.

answer.text: determining the base pairing sequences in nucleic acids
measuring the rate of active transport across biomembranes
separating cell organelles based on their sedimentation coefficient
analyzing the allowed conformations of proteins

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q03 - Physicochemical approach known as reductionist biology

questiontext.text: The study and understanding of living organisms by applying the concepts and techniques of physics and chemistry to describe biological processes in molecular terms is known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the definition of the physico-chemical approach to life
The Unit 3 introductory text states that analyzing living tissues for elements and compounds enables one to explain physiological and behavioural processes in molecular terms.

Step 2: Identify the specific terminology
This physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms is termed 'Reductionist Biology'.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, this physico-chemical approach is known as Reductionist Biology.

answer.text: Ecological Biology
Evolutionary Biology
Morphological Biology
Reductionist Biology

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q04 - First observation and description of a live cell

questiontext.text: Who among the following scientists first saw and described a live cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the historical discovery of live cells
Section 8.1 of the textbook states that Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell under the microscope.

Step 2: Contrast with other early discoveries
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831, whereas Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory, and Virchow introduced the concept of pre-existing cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek is the scientist who first saw and described a live cell.

answer.text: Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek
Robert Brown
Matthias Schleiden
Rudolf Virchow

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q05 - Discovery of nucleus as a cell organelle

questiontext.text: The nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall early observations of cellular structures
According to the NCERT text, the discovery of the nucleus within cells was achieved in 1831.

Step 2: Identify the scientist credited with the discovery
Robert Brown first described the nucleus as a distinct cellular entity in the year 1831.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by Robert Brown.

answer.text: Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek
Camillo Golgi
George Palade
Robert Brown

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q06 - Requirement of complete cellular structure for independent living

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements explains why a cell is considered the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the criteria for independent existence
Unicellular organisms are capable of independent existence and performing the essential functions of life.

Step 2: Identify the limitation of subcellular entities
The text explicitly asserts that anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living, which establishes the cell as the structural and functional baseline of life.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the fundamental nature of the cell is justified because anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living.

answer.text: Subcellular components isolated outside the cell can independently divide and reproduce indefinitely.
All metabolic reactions can occur in an abiotic environment without any cellular integrity.
Living phenomena are independent of the integrity of cellular organization.
Anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q07 - Observations of Matthias Schleiden on plant tissues

questiontext.text: In 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, concluded from his studies that:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Matthias Schleiden's professional background and observation
Matthias Schleiden was a German botanist who, in 1838, examined a large variety of plant specimens.

Step 2: Recall his specific conclusion
He observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which aggregate to form the various tissues of the plant.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Schleiden concluded that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant.

answer.text: all animal cells are delimited by an outer layer called the plasma membrane
new cells always arise de novo from non-cellular inorganic matter
the cell wall is uniquely absent in plant tissues
all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q08 - Unique character of plant cells found by Schwann

questiontext.text: Theodore Schwann (1839), based on his comparative studies on plant and animal tissues, concluded that a unique character of plant cells is the presence of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review Theodore Schwann's comparative studies
Theodore Schwann, a German zoologist, studied various animal cells and reported that they possess a thin outer layer known today as the plasma membrane.

Step 2: Identify his deduction regarding plant cells
When he extended his studies to plant tissues, he concluded that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character distinguishing plant cells from animal cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the unique character of plant cells identified by Schwann is the presence of a cell wall.

answer.text: a cell wall
a plasma membrane
a contractile vacuole
centrioles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q09 - Contribution of Rudolf Virchow to cell theory

questiontext.text: The original cell theory formulated by Schleiden and Schwann had a major limitation because it could not explain how new cells were formed. This was resolved by Rudolf Virchow (1855), who stated:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the deficiency in Schleiden and Schwann's cell theory
The early formulation of the cell theory by Schleiden and Schwann explained that living organisms are made of cells, but failed to explain the origin or formation of new cells.

Step 2: Examine Rudolf Virchow's 1855 addition
Rudolf Virchow first explained that cells divide and that new cells arise from pre-existing cells, encapsulated in the Latin aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula'.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Virchow resolved the limitation by proposing that new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).

answer.text: cells arise spontaneously by crystallisation from extracellular inorganic fluids
plant and animal cells lack any common fundamental cellular organisation
genetic material is formed de novo inside the cytoplasm during each division cycle
Omnis cellula-e cellula, meaning that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q10 - Tenets of cell theory as understood today

questiontext.text:
Cell theory as understood today includes which of the following combined principles?
I. All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
II. All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
III. Cells generate spontaneously from abiotic non-living matter.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the postulates of modern cell theory
Modern cell theory has two fundamental tenets: (i) all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells, and (ii) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Step 2: Evaluate statement III
Spontaneous generation from abiotic matter is completely rejected by the modern cell theory and Virchow's principle of biogenesis.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the modern cell theory comprises only statements I and II.

answer.text: Only I and III
Only II and III
I, II and III
Only I and II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q11 - Structural boundary difference in onion and cheek cells

questiontext.text: When comparing an onion peel cell and a human cheek cell under a microscope, which outer boundary arrangement is correctly identified?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the structure of a typical plant cell (onion peel)
The onion peel cell represents a typical plant cell and possesses a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary, with the plasma membrane situated directly beneath it.

Step 2: Recall the structure of an animal cell (human cheek cell)
Human cheek cells represent animal cells and lack a cell wall; their delimiting boundary is the outer plasma membrane alone.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the onion cell has a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary with the cell membrane within it, whereas the cheek cell has an outer membrane as its delimiting structure.

answer.text: Both onion peel cells and human cheek cells have a rigid outer cell wall enclosing the plasma membrane.
The human cheek cell possesses an outer cellulosic cell wall, while the onion peel cell has only an outer plasma membrane.
Neither cell type possesses a distinct cell membrane; both are directly bounded by naked cytoplasm.
The onion cell has a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary with the cell membrane just within it, whereas the human cheek cell has only an outer membrane as its delimiting structure.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q12 - Cytoplasm as the main arena of cellular activities

questiontext.text: The semi-fluid matrix that occupies the volume of the cell and serves as the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells is the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the semi-fluid matrix filling the cell
Section 8.3 describes the semi-fluid matrix occupying the volume of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells as the cytoplasm.

Step 2: Relate it to cellular activities
Various chemical reactions occur in the cytoplasm to maintain the cell in the living state, making it the primary arena of cellular metabolism.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the semi-fluid matrix acting as the main arena of cellular activities is the cytoplasm.

answer.text: cytoplasm
nucleoplasm
stroma
perinuclear space

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q13 - Locations of ribosomes in eukaryotic plant cells

questiontext.text: In a eukaryotic plant cell, ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found at which of the following intracellular sites?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the general nature and distribution of ribosomes
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound structures present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

Step 2: Identify specific locations in plant cells from the text
Section 8.3 states: 'Within the cell, ribosomes are found not only in the cytoplasm but also within the two organelles – chloroplasts (in plants) and mitochondria and on rough ER.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, ribosomes are present in the cytoplasm, within chloroplasts, within mitochondria, and on the surface of rough ER.

answer.text: Exclusively in the cytoplasm and inside the nucleus
Only on the outer surface of smooth ER and inside the Golgi cisternae
Only inside the nucleolus and within the central vacuole lumen
In the cytoplasm, inside chloroplasts, inside mitochondria, and on the surface of rough ER

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q14 - Dimensions of Mycoplasma, typical bacteria, and human RBCs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following biological dimensions mentioned in Chapter 8:
1. Length of Mycoplasma: approximately 0.3 µm
2. Length of typical bacteria: 3 to 5 µm
3. Diameter of human red blood cells: about 7.0 µm

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Verify the dimension of Mycoplasma
Mycoplasmas are the smallest living cells, having a length of only 0.3 µm.

Step 2: Verify the dimensions of bacteria and human RBCs
Typical bacteria are 3 to 5 µm in length, and human erythrocytes (RBCs) have a diameter of approximately 7.0 µm.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, all three statements (1, 2, and 3) correctly represent the dimensions specified in the NCERT text.

2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only

White blood cells are illustrated and labelled as having an 'amoeboid' shape.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, red blood cells are round and biconcave, while white blood cells are amoeboid.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q16 - Four basic morphological shapes of bacteria

questiontext.text: Bacteria exhibit four basic morphological shapes. Which pairing of shape name and description is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the four basic shapes of bacteria
The text defines the four basic bacterial shapes: bacillus (rod-like), coccus (spherical), vibrio (comma shaped), and spirillum (spiral).

Step 2: Evaluate the pairings
Vibrio corresponds precisely to comma shaped, while bacillus is rod-like and coccus is spherical.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the correct pairing is Vibrio – comma shaped.

answer.text: Vibrio – comma shaped

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q17 - Characteristics and phenotype conferred by bacterial plasmids

questiontext.text: In addition to the genomic DNA, many bacteria possess small circular DNA molecules called plasmids. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of plasmids?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the nature of plasmids in bacteria
Section 8.4 explains that in addition to the single circular genomic chromosome, many bacteria contain extrachromosomal small circular DNA molecules called plasmids.

Step 2: Identify the function of plasmid DNA
Plasmids confer unique phenotypic characters to host bacteria, a prime example being resistance to specific antibiotics, and are used to monitor transformation with foreign DNA.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, plasmids confer unique phenotypic characters to bacteria, such as resistance to antibiotics.

answer.text: They are enclosed inside a dedicated double-membrane envelope within the prokaryotic cytoplasm.
They are composed of linear single-stranded RNA molecules that code for ribosomal subunits.
They replace the genomic DNA during bacterial binary fission.
They confer unique phenotypic characters to bacteria, such as resistance to antibiotics.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q18 - Prokaryotes that lack a cell wall

questiontext.text: All prokaryotes possess a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane EXCEPT:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the cell boundary features of prokaryotes
Section 8.4 notes that prokaryotic cells generally have a rigid cell wall surrounding their plasma membrane.

Step 2: Identify the specific exception
The text explicitly states: 'All prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except in mycoplasma.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Mycoplasma is the prokaryote that lacks a cell wall.

answer.text: Blue-green algae
Bacillus
Spirillum
